gaps.node_type: preproc_def, preproc_ifdef, preproc_if, preproc_else, preproc_elif, preproc_endif, preproc_call, preproc_function_def, preproc_parameter, preproc_arg
gaps.missing: preprocessor conditional branches (ifdef/if/else) are not tracked as decision points or symbols; only preproc_include is consumed (imports)

gaps.node_type: block_expression, block_declarator, block_parameter, block_type, capture_specifier, capture, variable_declaration, function_declarator
gaps.missing: block-literal inner declarations are anonymous (generated names, no symbols); captured variables are not emitted as distinct symbols

gaps.node_type: objective_c_expression, objective_c_statement, superclass_reference, protocol_qualifiers, protocol_list, category_interface, category_implementation, selector, property_identifier
gaps.missing: obsolete/dead grammar-era names (pre-pinned-wasm aliases) — the pinned wasm has no such nodes; the analyzer never emits them. Documented to prevent future dead-literal regressions

decisions.question: The pinned grammar parses BOTH plain classes and categories as class_interface/class_implementation — the category is distinguished by an anonymous `(` token after the class name.
decisions.resolution: The analyzer scans the non-named children for the `(` token (pure AST, never source-text scanning). A category emits an Extension symbol (categoryName recorded) and NO inheritance edges; its methods are owned by the EXTENDED class. A plain class emits extends (the ONE superclass after the colon — never a protocol) + implements (protocols under parameterized_arguments). @interface + @implementation of the same class merge into one symbol (dedup key kind:owner:name without start line).

decisions.question: ObjC message sends `[receiver selector:arg]` — which node is the callee, and when is it an instantiation?
decisions.resolution: The selector is the FIRST identifier AFTER the receiver (never the receiver itself), so `[NSString stringWithFormat:]` calls stringWithFormat, not NSString. When the selector is alloc or new, the RECEIVER is the instantiated class ([[Foo alloc] init] resolves the receiver leaf through the nested inner message) — instantiates, not calls. Method-body scope only (the analyzer guards activeScope !== global, so file-scope messages are not emitted).

decisions.question: Blocks `^{ ... }` are anonymous — should they produce symbols?
decisions.resolution: No symbol (generated names are execution artifacts, same as C function pointers and closure literals elsewhere in the family). Their BODY message/calls ARE still captured (a block calling setHidden inside a method emits calls from the enclosing method scope).

decisions.question: ObjC dot-syntax property access (`self.next`, `w.next`, `self.origin.x`) parses as field_expression with a field_identifier — should these produce uses edges?
decisions.resolution: Yes for READS (managed-OO family contract — dart/swift/csharp emit uses for member reads): a field_expression inside a method body emits uses -> the field name with isFieldRead metadata. The LHS of an assignment_expression is a WRITE, never a read, so it is excluded (pure AST: the walk carries the parent type — never source-text scanning). This mirrors the C analyzer's field_access handling while honoring the family's read-vs-write distinction.
